questions.prompt: Why should date/time code make its time-zone assumptions explicit?
options: Date objects store the user’s preferred language automatically.
Every ISO-looking date string always uses local time.
Intl methods remove all differences between time zones.
Local time, UTC, daylight-saving rules and display locale can change the interpreted or displayed value.
questions.explanation: Use defined timestamps and explicit formatting/time-zone decisions for consistent results.

questions.prompt: What helps make a displayed date consistent across locales?
options: Choose an explicit locale and time zone when formatting the date.
Rely on the operating system default for every requirement.
Store a formatted display string as a universal timestamp.
questions.explanation: Intl.DateTimeFormat supports locale-aware display; the application still needs clear time-zone semantics.
